answer: A farm operator runs many names from one shared context, swapping attention as the tide demands, so each clone's half-finished work lives in one crowded memory. Freeze identities mid-task at random, hold them for hours, then demand resumption from their private step: state the next action and its reason before any output returns. A lone agent balanced on its own ledge recalls its intent; clones resume with generic steps or another name's details, like a lotus closed on the wrong pond. Mixing or missing marks the cluster, and keeping separate working memory per name erases the farm's saving.
